title: UAE Logistics Brief
lede: Oil crashed almost 9% after the US midterms, as Trump blamed petrol prices for his party's defeat and said he has no immediate plans to strike Iran. On the water nothing has eased yet: another tanker was hit off Oman and the queue of waiting ships grew to 197.

gauges.label: Brent crude, per barrel
gauges.note: Down 8.6% on Wednesday after the US midterms; near $118 last Friday (OilPrice.com, 4 Nov)

gauges.label: Ships holding position in the Strait and Gulf
gauges.note: Up from 158 a day earlier; AIS-visible, 00:00 UTC (Straits Daily Brief, 4 Nov)

gauges.note: Still the latest IMF PortWatch figure (Straits Daily Brief, 4 Nov)

gauges.label: Gulf oil exports in October
gauges.note: Down from 18.9m in September, about three-quarters of pre-war (Vortexa via OilPrice.com)

gauges.label: UAE airport seat capacity in October
gauges.note: Up 23% from June as airlines return (Gulf News, 4 Nov)

stories.headline: Oil crashes 9% after the US midterms; Trump says no immediate plan to strike Iran
body: Brent fell $8.94, or 8.6%, to $94.66 a barrel on Wednesday, its lowest since 4 September. WTI dropped 8.3% to $88.08. Trump blamed 'the gasoline price' for the Republican defeat, and Vance said the war was the reason for the losses.
Trump told the Financial Times there are no immediate plans to strike Iran. Iran's Supreme Leader said US hostility will persist whichever party holds power. There is still no deal on the strait.
stories.soWhat: The politics now point toward de-escalation, and fuel is falling fast. Prepare fuel surcharge cuts on air and road, but keep sea surcharges until ships move.

stories.headline: Another tanker hit off Oman as the ship queue jumps to 197
body: UKMTO reported a tanker hit by two projectiles into its engine room late on 3 November, about 14 nautical miles northeast of Lima, Oman. It is identified as the shadow fleet tanker Grit. Lloyd's List also reports the bulker Era S. was struck on 2 November while crossing the strait.

Iran's IRGC claims four more tankers hit mines near Oman; this is not verified. Tehran says it will give unlimited transit exemptions to ships from China, India, Iraq and Qatar, and has sent the US seven conditions for reopening. 197 ships were holding position on 4 November, up from 158.
stories.soWhat: New since yesterday: a second strike near Oman's coast and Iran's country-by-country exemptions. East coast bypass lanes still carry risk, so keep war-risk surcharges on all Gulf of Oman routings.
stories.source: The Maritime Executive; Straits Daily Brief

stories.headline: Etihad cancels Riyadh and Dammam cargo flights to 19 November; Jeddah returns on 6 November
body: Etihad has cancelled all passenger and cargo flights between Abu Dhabi and Riyadh, and Abu Dhabi and Dammam, through 19 November. The earlier cut ran to 5 November. Flights EY601 to EY604 to Jeddah resume on 6 November.

Other carriers are also out of Saudi Arabia: Lufthansa skips Riyadh to 18 November and Dammam to 30 November, and KLM both cities to 27 November. Emirates has also cancelled several Riyadh, Dammam and Jeddah flights.
stories.soWhat: UAE–Riyadh and Dammam air cargo stays short for two more weeks. Sell road for those lanes and price air on the capacity that is left.

stories.headline: BA lands in Dubai, but its Abu Dhabi route stays out until winter 2027-28
body: British Airways' first Heathrow flight landed in Dubai on 4 November on a Boeing 787-10. It flies once daily this winter and twice daily from summer 2027. Its Abu Dhabi service stays suspended until winter 2027-28. UAE airport seat capacity reached 7.2 million in October, up 23% from June.
stories.soWhat: New: Abu Dhabi will lack BA belly space for another year. Steer UK–Abu Dhabi express through Dubai and price it accordingly.

stories.headline: White Friday peak is three weeks away: 27 to 30 November
body: White Friday runs from Friday 27 November to Cyber Monday 30 November across the UAE, Saudi Arabia and the wider GCC, with most retailers campaigning through November. Rival Quiqup is already pitching same-day delivery, returns and UAE-to-KSA cross-border service to sellers for the peak.
stories.soWhat: Lock peak capacity and surcharges with e-commerce shippers now, while falling fuel gives room to offer sharp base rates.

competitors.name: Emirates SkyCargo
competitors.headline: AI Tech details: freighters for racks over 3.8 tons, cargo traffic up 5–6% this year
body: New detail on yesterday's launch: FreightWaves reports AI Tech adds priority loading, handling that keeps equipment upright and airport-to-airport monitoring. Emirates prefers freighters for server racks that often weigh more than 3.8 tons. Its air cargo traffic grew 5% to 6% year to date through October, and it runs 20 freighters with 23 expected by March.
competitors.soWhat: SkyCargo's offer stops at the airport. Sell Aramex Data Center Logistics as the door-to-data-hall layer on top of SkyCargo lift.

competitors.name: DP World
competitors.headline: Launches weekly China Africa Link from late November
body: DP World's shipping arm will start the weekly China Africa Link in late November. It calls at Shanghai, Ningbo, Nansha, Port Klang, Dar es Salaam, Maputo and Singapore, and backs it with more than $665 million of investment in the Maputo and Dar es Salaam terminals.
competitors.soWhat: DP World is building its own end-to-end freight lanes that skip the Gulf. Watch for it bundling ocean and forwarding on China–Africa trade we serve today.

competitors.name: Etihad Cargo
competitors.headline: Signs US cargo pact with Virginia targeting data centres, while its Saudi cargo flights stay grounded
body: Etihad Cargo signed an MoU with the Virginia Economic Development Partnership at TIACA's Air Cargo Forum in Miami to grow cargo through Washington Dulles. Focus sectors include pharma, perishables, energy and data centres. At home, its Riyadh and Dammam cargo flights are cancelled through 19 November.
competitors.soWhat: Both UAE carriers now court AI and data centre freight. Its Saudi gap is our road opening: offer Abu Dhabi–Riyadh and Dammam trucking to Etihad's stranded shippers.

opportunities.title: Cheaper fuel into peak season
opportunities.text: Brent is down to about $95. Use lower fuel costs to win White Friday and year-end air and road deals.

opportunities.title: Abu Dhabi–Saudi road freight
opportunities.text: Etihad's Riyadh and Dammam cargo flights stay off until 19 November. Push GCC trucking for those lanes.

opportunities.title: White Friday volumes
opportunities.text: Peak runs 27 to 30 November. Sign capacity and peak rates with e-commerce sellers this month.

opportunities.title: AI hardware, door to data hall
opportunities.text: Emirates and Etihad sell airport-to-airport. We can own the ground leg, customs and placement.

opportunities.title: Countries with Iranian transit exemptions
opportunities.text: If China, India, Iraq and Qatar ships get through first, sea capacity on those trades may return sooner. Track it lane by lane.

watchouts.title: Strikes near Oman
watchouts.text: Two ships have now been hit near Lima, Oman, in two days. Gulf of Oman lanes are not safe yet.

watchouts.title: Oil drop is not a deal
watchouts.text: Brent fell on politics, not on reopened lanes. The ship queue grew to 197.

watchouts.title: Fuel surcharge lag
watchouts.text: Customers will see a 9% oil fall in the news and ask for cuts before our costs fall.

watchouts.title: Saudi air capacity
watchouts.text: Etihad, Lufthansa, KLM and Emirates have Saudi flights cut, some to 30 November.

watchouts.title: Houthi claims on Riyadh airport
watchouts.text: The Houthis say they targeted King Khalid International; Saudi authorities did not confirm an attack.

moves.title: Draft December fuel surcharge cuts for air and road
moves.text: Model the drop at Brent near $95 and be ready to announce it, so customers hear it from us first.

moves.title: Hold sea war-risk surcharges
moves.text: Keep them on Fujairah, Khor Fakkan and Sohar routings after the tanker strike off Lima, Oman.

moves.title: Offer road cover for Riyadh and Dammam
moves.text: Contact shippers who used Etihad and Emirates belly to Riyadh and Dammam with a trucking option until 19 November.

moves.title: Close White Friday capacity deals
moves.text: Lock peak volumes and surcharges with top e-commerce sellers before 15 November.

moves.title: Pitch the ground leg on AI hardware
moves.text: Pair Data Center Logistics with SkyCargo AI Tech lift in proposals for Abu Dhabi data centre projects.

moves.title: Route UK–Abu Dhabi express via Dubai
moves.text: BA's Abu Dhabi flights stay off until winter 2027-28. Set Dubai connections and transit times for that lane.

note: Read from today's news. Check against our own numbers before acting.
